name: Silvretta Hochalpenstraße
kurzbeschreibung: Stunning alpine road with 58 hairpin bends leading from Tirol into the Montafon valley—offering breathtaking views of the Silvretta glaciers.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Silvretta-Hochalpenstraße ranks among the most spectacular and celebrated high-alpine scenic highways in the European Alps. Stretching 22.3 kilometers through 34 masterfully engineered hairpin bends, this mountain roadway connects Tyrol's Paznaun Valley across the 2,037-meter Bielerhöhe Pass to the Montafon valley in Vorarlberg. The crown jewel at the pass summit is the colossal Silvretta-Stausee reservoir: set against the glaciated amphitheater of the Silvretta Range—crowned by the jagged Piz Buin (3,312 m, Vorarlberg's highest peak) and the Silvrettahorn—the milky-turquoise glacial waters present an awe-inspiring sight. Originally constructed in the 1950s as a heavy transport route for Illwerke hydroelectric infrastructure, the pass today draws hundreds of thousands of road trippers, motorbikers, road cyclists, day hikers, and mountaineers each summer.

Route & Requirements

Bielerhöhe acts as a high-altitude outdoor staging ground for all abilities. The essential family trek is the Silvretta Lake Circuit: extending roughly 6.3 kilometers, a wide gravel pathway loops the shoreline with virtually no elevation gain, offering constant panoramas of hanging seracs and the retreating tongue of the Ochsental Glacier (1.5 to 2 hours walking time, easy grade T1). Mountaineers utilize the pass to access the historic Wiesbadener Hütte (2,443 m) up through the dramatic Ochsental valley (2.5 hours climb, 400 vertical meters, moderate grade T2), serving as the launchpad for roped glacial ascents of the Piz Buin. A unique marvel on the lake is the MS Silvretta: operating at over 2,000 meters elevation, it is the highest-altitude scheduled passenger motorboat in Europe. Given the high-alpine exposure well above the tree line, warm windproof outerwear and UV protection are mandatory. Leashed dogs are permitted on trails and aboard the scenic boat.

Visit & Arrival

Rail passengers travel via ÖBB mainline services into Landeck-Zams station. Connecting regional VVT bus line 260 journeys up the Paznaun valley via Ischgl and Galtür straight to the Bielerhöhe Silvrettasee terminus. Motorists arrive from the Inntal autobahn A12 and S16 expressway (exit Pians), following the B188 highway past Galtür to the toll plaza. The Silvretta High Alpine Road operates as a toll road, open seasonally from early June through late October (closed in winter). Expansive parking areas are located atop the pass.

Tips

Board the MS Silvretta for a 30-minute cruise across the glacial lake while the captain explains the monumental construction of the two gravity dams. Relax on the sun deck of Silvretta-Haus or Berggasthaus Piz Buin, savoring warm Tyrolean strudel and mountain cheeses with front-row glacier views.
preis: Mautgebühr Silvretta-Hochalpenstraße ca. 18–21 € pro PKW (Schifffahrt ca. 7 €)
oeffnungszeiten: Mitte Juni bis Mitte Oktober, täglich 6:00–20:00
